Everything else

When should I arrive?

Doors open at 2:30 PM and the ceremony starts at 3:00 PM sharp. Aim for 2:30 so you have time to park and find a seat.

What should I wear?

Whatever you're comfortable in. Just no white and no red. Casual or dressy, both work. Bring flats for the dance floor.

Is the wedding indoors or outdoors?

Both. The ceremony is outdoors. Cocktail hour is indoor and outdoor. Dinner and dancing are in the reception hall.

Can I bring my kids?

We're keeping the celebration to guests 12 and over. We adore your little ones. Consider this your night off.

We really do want you there, so if you need a sitter for the night, message us and we'll see what we can do.

Can I bring a guest?

If you have a plus one, it will be on your RSVP. If you don't have one and you need one, please message us as soon as possible.

Is there parking?

Yes. Ample parking on site.

What's being served?

Cocktail hour is a grazing table. Dinner is steak and chicken with baked potato, sweet potato and green beans.

At the bar there'll be two signature cocktails to choose from, plus beer and seltzers.

If you have a severe dietary allergy, please message us as soon as possible.

When do I need to RSVP by?

July 1, 2027. Please only RSVP yes if you know for certain you'll be there. We give the venue a final headcount for food, chairs and tables, so we need the number to be accurate.

The only thing we need from you

Please let us know by July 1, 2027. Only RSVP yes if you're certain you can make it. The venue needs an accurate headcount for food, chairs and tables.

Angela's version

We met at Dance XL, a country swing partner dance competition in Dallas. Neither of us planned to be there. Josh got free tickets. I was told about it last minute. We were both fairly new to country swing, and somehow, despite the same places, the same people and the same city in Vegas, we had never once crossed paths. Divine timing is real.

The first day, we met during a workshop and were instantly smitten. Somehow I knew that was the Josh our mutual connection had mentioned. We talked and laughed and stared at each other the entire class.

That connection had me thinking Josh might be quite the ladies' man. Turns out he just needed the right woman to respect, love and defend. I was living in Florida and had recently sworn off men. Turns out I just needed a man worthy of it.

After class I thought I was slick. I asked for a photo of the three of us, then said, "hey, let me send it to you, what's your number."

We spent practically the whole day together and Josh asked me out. The only thing open in that town at midnight was Applebee's, so our first date was Applebee's until 2 a.m. It felt like we were grilling each other with questions to make sure we were compatible. Then we danced in the parking lot.

The next morning he asked if I wanted coffee, my love language, and food. We spent the whole day at the event and danced by ourselves in the corner. That night we went to Cowboy Red River, a dance hall in Dallas, and had the most magical time. That's where he finally kissed me.

Sunday we realized the weekend was ending, so I changed my flight to stay one more day. We went to dinner and walked around Dallas.

Monday I had to work, so Josh memorized my Starbucks order from days earlier, ubered himself there and back, and brought it to me. He also, coincidentally, got me off Starbucks a year later.

We went to the airport five hours early and talked about the future the whole time. Josh said, "so, like, how do we do long distance?" I told him I'd come visit in three weeks.

I went home to LA and visited in three weeks exactly. I stayed two weeks and found myself not wanting to leave. The next time, he came to me and met my friends. We said I love you for the first time.

Josh started doing things he'd never done, like taking content on a beach. I started doing things I never did, like listening to a partner.

We spent the Fourth of July on a trip where I was convinced he was going to ask me to be his girlfriend. Plot twist: he still hasn't. So I skipped girlfriend and went straight to fiancée.

He introduced me to his dad and the rest of his family, and we started talking about moving in together. Late October 2024, I moved in. February 2025, we got a townhome. August 2026, we got engaged. He proposed doing what we love, dancing. The next day we went under contract on our home in Nashville.

Never did I think I'd end up with a man in the military. Never did Josh think he'd end up with a business woman who used to have hair extensions and bleach blonde hair. But here we are. God had such a presence in the timing of us meeting.

It is a privilege to love this man every day. He opened my eyes to the fact that there are real, great men out there who are worthy of your love, and that you don't have to do it all on your own. In fact, it's a lot more fun with a partner who matches your crazy, in the healthiest way. To our marriage, our future kids, and every adventure still to come.

Josh's version

It started in Dallas, Texas, at a dance competition I wasn't even supposed to attend. She was wearing a bright teal shirt, her hair all blonde with extensions, but I saw her—the real her. Not in the love-at-first-sight way you hear about in fairy tales and rom-coms, but in the way she carried herself and the way she spoke. As most of you know if you've met Angela, she is genuinely kind, caring, and intelligent. I saw that immediately, and when my chance came, I took it. I introduced myself and asked her to sit down and have a conversation with me.

Fortunately, I was at a point in my life that had room for something that wonderful. Of course, I had just sworn off dating altogether. I was over and done with it, and then she had to walk in. Truly, though, the timing was perfect for both of us. We had each been alone long enough to heal, long enough to know ourselves, and long enough to know exactly who we wanted in a partner. We just didn't think that person existed.

When she walked over and we introduced ourselves, I knew I had to get to know her more and see who she truly was. Lucky for me, she wanted to grill me with questions too. After a long night of dancing and talking, we ended up at Applebee's, the only place open late enough to sit down. We closed that place down, talking for hours, and then saw each other again the next day at the competition, Dance XL.

Throughout that weekend, I kept noticing more and more about her that made me think she would be a great partner in life. Then she changed her flight just to sit with me at the airport for three more hours, and that's when I said to myself, "Okay… this one is different." I couldn't possibly list every moment I've fallen deeper in love with her; that would turn into a novel. But the most important thing I can say is this: I still find moments that make me love her more and still fall even deeper.

In the "short" time we've been together, we've been through a lot of life: trials, tests, and taxes. It has been difficult and stressful at times, but there is no one else I would rather suffer through it with, and no one I would rather celebrate it with.

As for celebrations, there have been plenty: all of our dance trips together, a short camping excursion, and, of course, Italy. I told her I wouldn't propose there, but I still think she expected me to. These adventures have been amazing, but the ones that don't take us to another state or country are just as great, because it's all time spent with her; annoying her, loving her, and living this life, with her.

Like I said, I wasn't going to propose in Italy, because then that's all the trip would ever be: the time I proposed. Instead, we got to live it, enjoy it, and yes, even stress a little in it. It was after we got back to the States that I decided to get the ring, but that's a whole story in and of itself, for another time. I'll just say this to all the ladies out there: when your man gets down on one knee, please remember to actually say "Yes." It was amazing, and seeing her smile through happy tears is one of the highlights of my life.

All of this to say, our love story is still being written, as I think it should be. I'm sure there will be more tests and trials ahead, but we'll get through them. As cheesy as it sounds, it will be because of our love and respect for one another.
